entries.clue: Comic's dig about senior Tory leaders? (6)

indicatorNotes.about: One word placed about another goes round it, so JEER wraps the letters.
indicatorNotes.leaders: The leaders of a group walk at its front, so these are the first letters of senior and Tory.

blocks.note: a dig is a jibe, a jeer
first letters of senior and Tory

annotation.surface: A comedian taking a swipe at the grandees of the Conservative Party.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tories are the UK Conservative Party. Dig about reads as a jab aimed at the leaders; instead the jibe wraps round them.
annotation.definitionFit: A jester was the court comic, and the word is still used for any joker.

entries.clue: Minister Henry, um, getting screwed aboard plane (6,4)

indicatorNotes.getting screwed: Something screwed up is twisted out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order.
indicatorNotes.aboard: Passengers aboard a plane are inside it, so the rearranged letters go inside JET.

annotation.surface: A government minister called Henry fumbling his words while being fleeced on a flight.
annotation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt was Chancellor of the Exchequer, the UK finance minister, when this puzzle was set. Henry is only fodder here, not the minister's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Jeremy Hunt has held several UK cabinet posts, including Health, Foreign Secretary and Chancellor.

entries.clue: Waves of fantastic gains followed by loss – so backing out (7)

indicatorNotes.fantastic: Something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the letters of gains take a fanciful new order.
indicatorNotes.followed by: What follows comes after, so the letters from loss go after SIGNA.
indicatorNotes.backing: Backing is moving backwards, so SO is read right to left as OS.
indicatorNotes.out: Letters sent out leave, so OS is taken out of LOSS.

annotation.surface: Stock-market talk of wild gains followed by a slump and investors pulling out.
annotation.walkthrough: Waves here is a verb: someone who waves signals. LOSS loses its middle OS, which is SO turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: To wave at someone is to signal to them, so he waves means he signals.

entries.clue: Measure, then test for penetration (5)

indicatorNotes.then: Then means next in order, so TRY comes after EN.

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure of width

annotation.surface: Instructions for a builder or inspector: measure first, then check how far something goes in.
annotation.walkthrough: The en and the em are printers' measures that setters use constantly.
annotation.definitionFit: An entry is a going in, which is what penetration is.

entries.clue: Good to have youth support, as campaigning politicians often do (4-4)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes an action rather than naming it; glad-hand is the verb that fills it.

blocks.note: to give a hand is to support

annotation.surface: A party pleased to win over young voters, as politicians on the stump like to.
annotation.walkthrough: Youth support reads as backing from young voters; it splits into a youth and a support.
annotation.definitionFit: To glad-hand is to shake hands and greet people warmly, the routine of a politician on the campaign trail.

entries.clue: Ambassador wants member put away (6)

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
to put away food is to eat it

annotation.surface: A diplomat wanting a colleague locked up.
annotation.walkthrough: Member and put away both look political or penal; they are a limb and eating.
annotation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy, especially one sent by the Pope, so an ambassador.

entries.clue: Navalny's dead – insisted on reform (9)

indicatorNotes.on reform: To reform something is to form it again, so the letters are put together in a new order.

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees

annotation.surface: News of Alexei Navalny's death, with a call for change in Russia.
annotation.walkthrough: Alexei Navalny, the Russian opposition leader, died in prison in February 2024. The 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Navalny was Russia's best-known dissident, an opponent of the Kremlin.

entries.clue: Not pro-Europe, in brief, after one's on carpet (7)

indicatorNotes.in brief: Something in brief is cut short, so Europe is shortened to EUR.
indicatorNotes.after: After means coming later, so EUR goes after the rest.
indicatorNotes.on: In a down clue what is on something sits above it, so A goes before MAT.

blocks.note: a mat is a small carpet
EUR is the short form of Europe

annotation.surface: A Eurosceptic politician being hauled up in front of the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: Not pro-Europe reads as Eurosceptic, but the hyphen is a trick: Not pro is the definition, and Europe is wordplay. On the carpet means being reprimanded.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain opposite: pro is short for professional, and an amateur does the same thing without pay.

entries.clue: Wet politician's after lawyer (4)

indicatorNotes.after: After means coming later, so MP comes after DA.

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

annotation.surface: A feeble moderate politician chasing a legal job.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics a wet is a moderate, soft-line Conservative, which is where the surface points.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: damp is a mild degree of wet, while the surface borrows the British political sense of wet, a soft moderate.

entries.clue: Rambling politician's turn to get sack? (7)

blocks.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle

annotation.surface: A long-winded MP whose turn has come to be fired.
annotation.walkthrough: Get the sack means be fired, but here sack is only a bag.
annotation.definitionFit: A windbag talks at length and says little, like a rambling politician.

entries.clue: Just a prison block for Liz Truss and co? (5-4)

blocks.note: a prison is divided into wings

annotation.surface: A suggestion that a prison block is the proper place for Liz Truss and her allies.
annotation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022 and leads the Conservative right.
annotation.definitionFit: Truss and her allies are on the right of the Conservative Party, so the label right-wing fits them.

entries.clue: Host was like a fish, drinking last of beer (5)

indicatorNotes.drinking: What you drink goes inside you, so R goes inside SWAM.
indicatorNotes.last of: The last of something is its final part, so beer gives its final letter.

annotation.surface: A host at the bar who drank like a fish, down to the dregs of the beer.
annotation.walkthrough: Host looks like the one throwing the party; it is a great number, as in a host of people.
annotation.definitionFit: A host and a swarm are both large crowds.

entries.clue: (& 18dn.) Emulated – oh my! badly – just like a question-dodging politician (5)

indicatorNotes.badly: Something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order.

annotation.surface: Someone copying an evasive politician rather poorly, to the speaker's dismay.
annotation.walkthrough: Oh my! reads as an exclamation, but its letters are fodder along with emulated.
annotation.definitionFit: Mealy-mouthed means afraid to speak plainly, exactly how a politician dodges a question.

entries.clue: A political con? (8)

blocks.note: read as describing a scheme cooked up by politicians, meant as a person held for political reasons
read as a swindle, meant as short for convict, a prisoner

annotation.surface: What sounds like a scam pulled by a politician.
annotation.walkthrough: Con looks like a swindle, the usual charge against politicians; it is short for convict, and a political prisoner is a detainee.
annotation.definitionFit: A political detainee is someone held in custody for political reasons, a political con in the convict sense.

entries.clue: Given the Opposition party treatment: done to death? (10)

blocks.note: a pun: made into the Opposition party, which was Labour when this was set
said of a point argued far past its useful life

annotation.surface: A question of whether handing things to the Opposition would kill them off.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a pun: BE LABOURED, made Labour, the Opposition party when this was set.
annotation.definitionFit: A point belaboured has been gone over far too long, done to death.

entries.clue: 'Hot Lips' and a resurrected M*A*S*H final part (8)

indicatorNotes.resurrected: Something resurrected is brought back in a new form, so the letters return in a new order.

annotation.surface: Talk of a revival of M*A*S*H, with its character Hot Lips back.
annotation.walkthrough: Hot Lips Houlihan is a character in M*A*S*H, which stands for Mobile Army Surgical Hospital; its final part is the H.
annotation.definitionFit: The last word the H of M*A*S*H stands for is Hospital.

entries.clue: Not looking yourself, pissed, noticing nothing (9)

indicatorNotes.pissed: Pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order.

annotation.surface: So drunk you look unlike yourself and notice nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Not looking yourself suggests seeming unwell; it means disguised.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has disguised themselves, so is not looking like themselves.

entries.clue: (& 29ac.) "Gargoyle with ego", law-bending political maverick (6)

indicatorNotes.bending: What is bent is pulled out of shape, so the letters are pulled into a new order.

annotation.surface: An insulting nickname for a rule-bending political maverick.
annotation.walkthrough: George Galloway is a veteran left-wing British MP, expelled from Labour and elected for Rochdale in 2024. Law-bending reads as a description of him; law is fodder and bending the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Galloway has spent decades as a contrarian outsider to the main parties, a political maverick.

entries.clue: see 12ac. (7)
No expert, on reflection, Kamala Harris? (6)

indicatorNotes.on reflection: A reflection is a mirror image, so ON is read backwards.

blocks.note: she was Vice President of the United States

annotation.surface: A dismissive judgment that Kamala Harris, thinking it over, is no expert.
annotation.walkthrough: Kamala Harris was US Vice President, so she stands for VICE; the question mark flags that shortcut.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a novice is a beginner, someone who has not yet gained expertise.

entries.clue: Victor, extremely impartial, accepts 'threesome equals abuse' (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: The extremes of a word are its ends, so impartial gives its first and last letters.
indicatorNotes.accepts: What is accepted is taken in, so TRIO goes inside IL.

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
first and last letters of impartial
a trio is a group of three

annotation.surface: A man called Victor, scrupulously fair, conceding that a threesome counts as abuse.
annotation.walkthrough: The quote marks make threesome equals abuse look like one statement; equals only links wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Vitriol is bitter, savage criticism, which is abuse.

entries.clue: What's wrong with Dicky getting a wrap? (8)

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
dicky is British slang for unwell or weak, as in a dicky heart

annotation.surface: Asking what ails someone called Dicky who is being wrapped up.
annotation.walkthrough: Dicky's capital makes it look like a name; it is the adjective. Tort is the legal word for a civil wrong.
annotation.definitionFit: A tortilla is the flat bread used as a wrap.

entries.clue: Victim of pot? Chuck rest out (7)

indicatorNotes.out: Out means out of order, so the letters of rest are rearranged.

blocks.note: to chuck is to throw, lob

annotation.surface: Someone harmed by cannabis being told to give up relaxing.
annotation.walkthrough: Pot looks like cannabis; it is a lobster pot, the trap they are caught in.
annotation.definitionFit: Lobsters are caught in pots and often cooked in one too.

entries.clue: Ropey thing's scandalous affair (6)

indicatorNotes.scandalous: What is scandalous is shocking and improper, so the letters are shocked out of their proper order.

annotation.surface: A shoddy something turning out to be a scandalous affair.
annotation.walkthrough: Ropey is British slang for poor quality, but here it means rope-like.
annotation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm fibre used like string or rope for tying and weaving.

entries.clue: Inactive males only wanting new false tan (8)

indicatorNotes.false: What is false is not genuine, so tan is not in its real order.

blocks.note: a stag party or stag night is for men only

annotation.surface: Lazy men who just want a fresh fake tan.
annotation.walkthrough: A stag do is a British bachelor party, men only.
annotation.definitionFit: Stagnant means not moving or developing, inactive.

entries.clue: Being penetrated by sailor: unduly prohibited (5)

indicatorNotes.Being penetrated by: What is penetrated has something pushed into it, so AB goes inside TOO.

blocks.note: an AB is an able seaman

annotation.surface: A saucy line about a sailor that sounds like it breaks a taboo.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay comes first and unduly sits right beside the definition, so it is easy to read unduly prohibited as one phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taboo, from Tongan tapu, means banned by custom or social rule.

entries.clue: Pissed but not likely to lash out (5)

blocks.note: lash out here means spend freely, so this is someone mean with money

annotation.surface: A drunk who stays peaceful.
annotation.walkthrough: Lash out suggests violence, but here it means spend freely, so not likely to lash out is stingy. Pissed is British slang for drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Tight means both drunk and mean with money.

entries.clue: Roger has droop – holding his head (4)

indicatorNotes.holding: What holds something has it inside, so SAG goes round H.
indicatorNotes.head: The head of a word is its first letter.

annotation.surface: A man called Roger with an embarrassing droop.
annotation.walkthrough: Roger and shag are both British slang for having sex; Roger's capital makes it look like a name.
annotation.definitionFit: To roger and to shag are both British slang for having sex.

entries.clue: Republic's call for attention over controversial technology (getting tense) (5)

indicatorNotes.over: HI is spread over the other letters, going round them.
indicatorNotes.getting: Getting means acquiring, so AI takes T on.

blocks.note: hi is a greeting to catch someone's eye

annotation.surface: A republic's appeal for notice over a disputed technology, and things getting fraught.
annotation.walkthrough: Getting tense suggests nerves; tense is the grammar term, abbreviated T.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Haiti, sharing the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, has been an independent republic since 1804.

entries.clue: Crafty thing, er, after drug-swallowing scare (9)

indicatorNotes.swallowing: What is swallowed ends up inside, so E goes into FRIGHT.
indicatorNotes.after: After means coming later, so ER comes after the rest.

annotation.surface: A sly type hesitating after a drugs scare.
annotation.walkthrough: Crafty looks like cunning; it means being a craft, a vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo ship or plane, a craft.

entries.clue: see 17ac. (8)
Saved flailing Tories not one day (6)

indicatorNotes.flailing: To flail is to thrash about wildly, so the letters thrash into a new order.
indicatorNotes.not: Not means without, so one is taken out of Tories.

annotation.surface: Floundering Conservatives being rescued, just not one day.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tories are the UK Conservative Party. One is I, the Roman numeral, removed before shuffling.
annotation.definitionFit: Saved and stored both mean kept for later.
